reviews.text: 丢个大师难度全成就通关视频 BV1d7iTecEvp 感觉11关开始数值把控没有之前好了，很多关卡基本没有难度，关卡之中凑数的波次也有不少，经常原封不动就可以通过下一波次，这种情况一直持续到21关才恢复了高难。 后面3个boss关卡设计也不太行，boss波次甚至都不如前面波次给的压力大。 银行是一个很讨厌的东西，你必须在最终波次前扣紧自己手里的每一块钱用来吃利息，以防止在最终波次过不去后必须从头重打。 加分项也有，比如很多人吐槽高难只有唯一解，其实这只存在于前面几关。打完全成就后我去翻看了看另一位b站up和油管一位up的视频，很少会有解法完全一致的。例如14关我的解法完全偏离了地图设计意图，也一样过关了。哪怕是最难的旧21关（难到制作组直接修改了地图，新版本变得简单了很多），油管上也给出了和我不同的解法。 ————————以下写于游玩至第10关时——————————————— 这不是爽游，这不是爽游，这不是爽游，重要的事情说三遍，想爽的建议换个游戏。 这游戏没有局外成长，没有乱七八糟的刷子要素、肉鸽要素，就是纯粹的策略塔防。 如果喜欢这类有限条件下寻解的策略塔防的话，推荐下X-Morph：Defense -机翻有点难绷 -帧数波动会导致怪在极限距离多A一下或者少A一下，这也是为什么有时候一模一样的操作过不去，不过这也是这类游戏的通病了。[spoiler] 明日方舟也干了 [/spoiler]根本原因是游戏运行是按帧运行的（所有游戏都这样），比如你第59帧的时候极限距离A出去了，但是如果帧数波动导致直接从第58跳到了第60帧，那么怪就会走出范围（大致逻辑是这样的）。然后这游戏优化并不好，我电脑玩这游戏发热和3A大作一样……建议把垂直同步关了，特效调最低，比较极限的关卡开0.4倍速。 -略贵的价格 +优秀的数值把控，你必须仔细分析地形和敌人的种类，在有限的资源下选择正确的塔和正确的位置才能完美通关。在后面越来越复杂的关卡中，玩家的可操作性也在上升，完美通关容错率其实没那么低。通过摆放地基反复分割敌人可以让你的容错大幅度上升，解法很多时候也不止一种。当然找到正确的塔和正确的位置仍是必须的。 +类魂的教程，这里并不是指明面的教程，而是游戏通过关卡设计让你理解一些塔防游戏的重要逻辑。拿第一关弓箭手举例，大多数不玩此类游戏的人会认为右边拐角处比左上更适合输出。然而实际上的输出时间为塔覆盖路径+怪物经过次数*怪物队伍长度，左上位置怪物会两次经过攻击范围，因此这才是大师难度的正确解。后面的很多关卡都会或多或少的教会你这些塔防的底层逻辑。（当然如果你没有悟到，在大师难度就会一直卡住） 结论：这无疑是塔防爱好者不可错过的自虐佳作。 [spoiler] 就凭这游戏的单体减速塔能雨露均沾也值得一个好评，好多塔防游戏的单体减速塔要么永远只会攻击走在最前方的怪，要么锁定一个敌人之后打死了才换目标，实在是吐槽无力 [/spoiler] 最后讲点小技巧，希望对各位还在自虐的玩家有帮助 1.塔升级是会重置攻击的，尤其是像重弩这种攻击间隔比较长的塔，通过升级可以实现3连发。 2.一般如果是在后点守的话，前点的路径可以晚一点造。面对压力比较大的关卡，在一半怪通过之后再造地基实现分割。之后还可以通过造减速塔实现二次分割。当然如果不做不拆塔成就的话可以反复用，做成就的话只能分割两次。 4.礼物的地基拆除时不抠钱，扩大田地或者反复分割敌人的时候可以省钱。 5.飞镖不止可以打虫巢，也能点杀加血怪。在投石塔面对怪堆带加血怪的时候很有用。 6.游戏里似乎没有说明，一格的距离是10，塔的距离是以正方形中心为起点计算的
出怪做的很恶心，塔的针对性太强了还没aoe。不过能读档到每波，这也就唯一优点了 简中 繁中都是机翻

Don't expect a TD like the WC3 maps. This is not a TD, this is a puzzle game were you need to retry each waves to find out which solution the dev had in mind. Towers have no real upgrade (3lvl + 1mega upgrade for 1 tower per map) so there's not much replayability/things to try. Also, why is my 3080 running at 100%. I need to disable vsync and lock my fps at 30.

强迫症玩家不建议入手这款游戏，想无伤通关基本没有容错，结果就是一款塔防游戏硬生生做成了解密游戏，只能在正确的时间在正确的位置摆上正确的塔才能无伤，说实话我真的不想玩塔防去点开别人的视频抄作业。 原因是游戏针对性做的太强的同时数值还扣的很死，很多塔打护甲怪根本不掉血。就算你知道什么怪要用什么塔针对，但只要塔的位置、路线的设计有那么一点点的不合理就会漏怪恶心你。 游戏可以根据地形设计路线的创意非常棒，但低到离谱的穿甲数值让人玩起来非常难受。

The game is fun at first, but difficulty spikes quite a bit after a while, to the point that instead of being a casually fun TD game, it is extremely difficult to complete without doing things in a very exact way (the way the devs want you to). There isn't really a lot of fun involved after the first few maps as it turns into trying to figure out exactly what the dev had in mind. I'd much rather have it be a fun TD, or at least provide a difficulty level for having fun, where you have more starting gold, or enemies drop extra gold, etc...

This game is annoyingly difficult and the controls are bad. It starts by being almost too easy then quickly gets annoyingly difficult even on the easiest setting. The limitations of the map layouts and the fact that you cant modify your towers aiming priority makes the game annoying. A casual setting could be added to make it playable. Also, the flying mob and the bug mobs are just annoying because of the extremely limited amount of towers. Each tower can only be upgraded two times, unless its an elite and that even more limits your defense strategy. It has nice graphics but a bit too dark on the levels I'm at now. I usually love TD's but I like the building up, finding a strategy that works and destroying the enemies with a good combination of towers. Here I just feel I dont have enough money, space or power to win.

I hate this game. And i've also played it a lot more than 2 hours since i've been playing in offline mode, so it's not just an initial impression or lack of understanding of the game that makes me hate it. The review below should show that I've got some indepth knowledge of the game. It's not a tower defense game; it's a puzzle game. There's one, and only one, way to complete each level. You have to build a certain tower in a specific way, in a specific order. The entire game is "master says, monkey do," where you are the monkey—if you don't play exactly as you've been ordered, you lose instantly. And the loss happens regardless of the difficulty level. I played on the easiest difficulty with the new helper feature that makes the game easier, and still got totally dominated and crushed every time, every map. And the worst part is that the game is designed for this puzzle-style gameplay because it's possible to restart the map from each wave. You can press escape during a level and then press "restart from wave x," so the idea is that you should restart each level and wave multiple times to optimize your play. Then, of course, the game has interest too. If you play tower defense games to build towers, stop right here—this game wants you to build as few towers as possible to maximize interest so you can get more money. Who likes interest in tower defense games? "Yeah, let's buy a tower defense game that’s about building towers... and then not build towers?" Did you beat wave 4? Restart wave 4 but build one less tower or one less upgrade to see if you can save 10 gold and get even more interest. How is this fun? The maps are also worthless, designed to tease you. Oh, you want to build a maze that goes around two turns? Almost, it’s just one tile short. Every map in the game: "Okay, new map, here I can build a circle so the creeps must go around the circle twice," nope, there's a sand pit right in the middle so it’s just impossible to build it that way. The maps are designed to mess with you and tease you; first, they probably made a normal map, then they investigated how to build different mazes on it, and then they threw in sand, lava, and other trash to mess with you and prevent you from building how you want. As I said earlier, this is the biggest issue with the game: you play as you're ordered, or you don't play at all. The towers are okay; there are some towers with interesting designs, but the upgrades are boring and barely do anything, except for the last one that upgrades the tower to elite status. However, the problem is the same as before: "master orders, monkey do." You can't have as many elite upgrades as you want, just a certain number per map, and not only that, you don’t even get to choose which towers you want to upgrade to elite, it's already been decided for you. On level 7, you can only upgrade the ice tower to elite, nothing else, while on level 11 you can upgrade two archers and a catapult tower to elite. But if you want to upgrade your ice tower to elite on level 11? Too bad, you can’t, the master hasn’t ordered it, so the monkey can't do it. On level 11, you must play in a certain way, and no other way. Here, you as the player don’t decide how to play, the master has already decided for you. The game has a positive rating of 88% as of this review, and I can't understand why. I love tower defense games and have played tons of them, both here and on flash sites when I was younger, but this is, as I said, not a tower defense game, it’s a puzzle game. I usually finish every game I’ve bought since I’ve spent money on them, but this is one of the few I will not finish. You just get angry every time you start it and try a map, even on the easiest difficulty with the help feature on… So don’t be fooled by the high rating of this game; it's given by people who’ve only played for an hour or two and think "well, there’s nothing wrong here," or by people who like puzzle games. Only buy this game if: 1. You like puzzle games. 2. You enjoy optimizing things, playing the same map over and over, every wave repeatedly, to complete it with as much money in the bank as possible via the interest system. 3. You like following orders, you're a follower, not a leader. You enjoy when everything is already planned for you, and you just do as you're told. 4. You've played every other tower defense game on Steam. There are tons of better TDs out there. Alternatively, if you want to save some money, watch a walkthrough of the game on YouTube because that person playing in the video is playing exactly how you will. As mentioned before, there's one, and only one, way to win every level, so if you'd bought the game, you’d play it exactly like in the YouTube video. If you want to beat the level, that is."

Defense Grid and Kingdom Rush are much better. Artisan TD is about building a perfect maze, and the tricks in the levels make you start over and over. For example, at wave 5 some flyers went off board, out of reach of all but one kind of turret, placed against that edge. You couldn't expect that so you restart taking that into account. The information about coming waves is often hidden. You have to restart, over and over.

Rarely have I spend this much time on a tower defence game. I played bloons, kingdom rush, plants vs zombies but this one beats them all for me hands down. Heavily underrated. I looked this game up on reddit and the sub for it had 21 members, this game deserves a lot better. it's true that some waves seem to have a very specific solution but finding that solution is fun for me. no microtransactions, no AAA gaming ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Just a simple concept and a very decent game. The only negative for me is that you cant just delete your progress and restart the game. I had to get out of my way to delete the files on my pc and get that to sync with the cloud. I go trough this levels by difficulty. Starting with adventure to get to know the map a bit, beat veteran after that, go to prince nightmare mode and then finish with nightmare mode itself. Only then I get to the next level. I really recommend this one and I hope it'll gain more popularity so they make a sequel.

I have very mixed feelings about this game. On one hand, it has beautiful graphics, very pleasant music (reminiscent of the compositions from Fable), a good variety of towers and monsters and an almost perfect save system for this type of game - saving at every wave and allowing you to replay ANY stage. The gameplay can be truly engaging, especially on Veteran difficulty when you’re trying to complete a map perfectly. There’s also the ability to build your own custom labyrinth. On the other hand, there are constant crashes (the game is made on a pretty unstable version of Unity - during the first two weeks my sessions lasted about 30 minutes; later they stretched to 3–4 hours before crashing, even though I didn’t notice any patches; the autosave system is the only thing that saved it from a technical refund), absolutely ridiculous bugs (this is the first Tower Defense game I’ve seen where towers just don’t shoot at enemies at all, they simply run across the map until you restart the game) and insanely high difficulty on Nightmare (you LITERALLY have to memorize the number of enemies in each wave and replay some waves over and over just to squeeze out 2–3 extra shots). There are also “goodbye mental health” level achievements; a mechanic where the game doesn’t show how many enemies are in a wave (for example: it says there will be dragons, you place a rocket tower, only a couple appear - you replay the wave because you actually needed money for something else; or it says there will be runners - dozens of them and you end up replaying 2–3 waves because you didn’t have enough resources), and my personal favorite: the game introduces a new enemy, but only explains how to deal with it one wave later - so go ahead and replay. SO... If you enjoy hardcore challenges, brutally difficult achievements, and yelling through your teeth “what are you even shooting at, you dumbass?” - welcome. If you don’t like high difficulty, value your mental health, or might smash your keyboard and mouse in frustration - better stay away. If you’re a casual player who doesn’t care about achievements, prefers lower difficulty, or doesn’t want to dive deep into maze-building and tower synergy mechanics - this game will likely exhaust you.

The Good Artisan TD has decent depth on paper, and tower synergies and deterministic waves should make it a planner’s dream. The core mechanics are solid and the game isn't bad. If you like building systems, the tools are all here. The Problem: Nightmare Perfect Isn’t Hard, It’s Opaque Nightmare difficulty kills what makes tower defense satisfying. There’s a fixed solution and near zero error margin, and theoretically optimal tower placement will leak. Winning requires specific “trick” placements that are anti-intuitive - you have to put towers in mathematically bad spots now to counter a single enemy type 2 waves later. Or have a tower 1 tile off optimal if you want to kill the last guy in this wave because of pathing and HP pools. You don’t beat levels through intelligence or adaptation. You beat them through trial-and-error. A leak on wave 5 is usually caused by a placement on wave 3, with no feedback in between. So you replay multiple minutes at a time until you brute-force the designer’s intended solution. The Result There’s no “aha!” moment. No transferable skill between maps. The winning builds often look ugly and imperfect because you’re not solving a system - you’re memorising a sequence. When you finally win, the feeling isn’t “I’m clever,” it’s “finally that’s over.” For Whom? If you enjoy rote memorisation and don’t mind replaying to find one exact solution, you’ll click with Nightmare. If you don't mind imperfect wins or lower difficulty runs, this isn't bad at all. But if you play TD for puzzle-solving and the satisfaction of watching a well-designed fortress work, this will likely frustrate you. Verdict: 3/5 Fair if non-innovative foundation ruined by difficulty design that confuses “obscure” with “clever.” It’s trivial to beat eventually, but you won’t feel smart doing it.

TL;DR: It's not terrible but pretty meh. Has a loooot of issues, especially around communicating information to the player. Can still be fun, but a rough experience The Bad: - Broken (feels like a bad translation into english) and/or ambiguous english ("Arrival Portal" is what the enemies go towards, it would've been much more clear if it was called something like "Target Portal" in addition to the "Starting Portal" where monsters spawn from) - Inconsistent language: The tutorial refers to "goo" towers or something, when the tower they are referring to is called "Ice Tower". Same thing for mentioning "crossbows", the tower is called "Arbalest Tower". Which is technically accurate, but it's unnecessarily confusing, stick to the same terminology - No numbers on health of enemies remaining. The visual hp bar will go down, same for armor, but you won't get numbers. You also won't see any active effects listed like slowdowns - With several sets of spawning and target portals, you don't know which portal enemies are going towards. Mousing over or at the very least clicking on them should show their path. Generally, you only see enemy paths when you are constructing walls, mousing over portals as well as enemies should show paths - So many other places where i would like more information - Would prefer to not use colours and instead text or symbols to communicate wave types (i still don't know what red means after 5-6 maps) - Dumb targeting: Several towers will shoot at the same enemy even if only one of them would kill the enemy already - Archers will also keep shooting the same enemy, even if it's a tank they can never kill, while flying enemies just fly directly overhead....frustrating! Archers should swap targets with flyers around because that is LITERALLY their main reason for existing! - DLSS even on quality setting causes flickering of outlines - Barely any hotkeys, not even for upgrading which is super important also during waves so where time is critical. You cannot pause the game during waves either to build or upgrade! - If you want perfect runs, be prepared to restart waves a lot later on to try and figure out how you can possibly make it work. Just surviving isn't so difficult on veteran, but perfect scores are not fun to get The Good: - Flying enemies feel balanced. They provide a challenge by flying over walls, without feeling too difficult to manage if you plan ahead. Nice! - Aside from the difficulty to get perfect runs, the tower variety (so far) is nothing groundbreaking, but it works well enough. - Enemy variety is interesting. I liked the insectoids with their special effect in particular, haven't seen those in a TD game before. New enemy types will be introduced frequently - Different maps do make you think about how you want to build your maze, although it feels like it could potentially be difficult if you don't see the (near) optimal way - The visuals are nice, i like how the wall segments connect to each other instead of just forming separate towers Overall Artisan TD is held back quite a bit with the lack of polish, QoL and information, which make it more frustrating than it should be. After getting the first 10 or so maps on perfect, i'll probably not come back to this game. It's not a terrible game, but i would probably feel ripped off if i hadn't gotten it through humble choice. I certainly would not want to pay 16.49€

一句話先講結論，我會把Artisan TD 歸類成「很漂亮、很吃腦、很看你吃不吃這套」的迷宮型塔防。 重點是利用地形、特殊格子、農田經濟跟塔位，去把怪物逼進你設計好的迷宮裡；再加上 30 張手工地圖、10+ 可升級防禦塔，整體玩起來就很像一款被精心雕過的棋盤式 TD，而不是靠隨機 build 滾雪球的那種。初期會覺得「能自己決定擺設、創造迷宮」這件事很有意思，但同時也坦白說，玩幾關後真的會開始覺得很燒腦。 它最明顯的優點，是質感真的比很多獨立塔防來得突出。 但它的缺點也是真的很難裝沒看到。Steam 負評幾乎都繞著同一個核心打：很多人覺得它很容易變成 「one solution for every map」，甚至直接罵它是 「puzzle game disguised as a TD」；也就是說，假如你想要的是比較自由、可以靠自己愛用流派慢慢磨過去的塔防，這款很可能會讓你覺得綁手綁腳。連喜歡它的玩家都有人抱怨「塔的變化與升級性太少、關卡太少」，Gameindustry 也點出它少了不少進階 TD 常見的跨關卡升級與長線成長系統。 所以最後我的建議會很直接：如果你喜歡的是迷宮造路、完美通關、一直優化同一關配置的解題感，那Artisan TD其實值得玩，CP 值不差。反過來說，如果你追求的是塔種很多、玩完主線還能靠 endless 或地圖編輯器一直刷下去，那它現在就沒那麼對味。簡單講，這款比較像塔防裡的「設計感小品」，不是那種萬用型、誰來都能吃的神作。

This is a weird one. I like the enemies, I like the mazing, I like the towers, the music is nice, the visuals are good, and the ability to "rewind" to prior waves is a potential leap forward for the entire genre. However, as great as these things are, this game feels like a puzzle game masquerading as a tower defense game. Yes, you do all of the tower defense "stuff," but on quite a few maps, any decision to use certain maze/tower layouts other than what the developers intended will lead to almost certain doom, even on the standard difficulty without the easier settings. To explain a bit better, I realize that certain TD maps often require certain towers, and that you shouldn't be able to just build your maze willy-nilly like a fool. This isn't what I'm talking about doing in Artisan TD. You can come up with your best design with logic and reason behind it, and try to plan for future waves with good tower placement, but there is only so much you can do. Ultimately, fairly early on in the game, you will have to restart over and over again, trying a different starting tower, maze design, or tower placement, just to get through the first wave. Each subsequent wave will be much the same. Thankfully, the ability to rewind several waves instead of starting over completely makes this less painful, but eventually, this entire process just became a slog. I was glad to be done with the game so I could put it behind me and never play it again. It just made me want to play better tower defense games again instead.

I have to admit, I think I picked well with this one. I sat down intending to record a first look video and ended up playing for just over 42 minutes, making my way through the first seven levels. The only reason I stopped was because I had a video to finish and upload. Had I simply been playing for myself, I could quite happily have carried on working through the rest of the campaign. The thing that immediately grabbed me was the classic maze-building gameplay. As someone who has been playing Tower Defence games for many years, this reminded me of what first got me hooked on the genre. Rather than simply dropping towers beside a fixed path, you're encouraged to build and shape the maze yourself, making every placement feel important. It has that satisfying old-school strategic feel that I really enjoy. The opening levels are clearly designed as tutorials, so they do feel a little more restrictive than I'd normally like. At times it can feel as though the game is gently steering you towards the intended solution rather than letting you experiment freely. However, I don't really see that as a major criticism because the larger maps later in the game look like they'll offer much more freedom once all the mechanics have been introduced. 👍 What I liked Classic maze-building Tower Defence gameplay. Easy to learn but still satisfying to play. A clean presentation that keeps the focus on strategy. I genuinely wanted to keep playing after recording. A great choice for anyone who enjoys traditional Tower Defence games. 👎 What could be better The early tutorial levels feel a little rigid. There are fewer towers, upgrades and maps than some of the genre's biggest names. At the current full price, I think it feels a little expensive for the amount of content available. That last point is probably my only real reservation. I bought the game during a sale for £6.52 and at that price I think it represents very good value. At its current full price of £14.49 though, I personally think it's a little ambitious when compared with games such as Defense Grid 2 and the GemCraft series, which offer considerably more content and replayability through larger selections of towers, upgrades, maps and wave combinations. Overall though, I really enjoyed my time with Artisan TD. It scratches that old-school Tower Defence itch extremely well, the maze-building is genuinely satisfying, and before I knew it more than 40 minutes had disappeared. If you're a fan of classic Tower Defence games, especially those that let you build your own mazes, I would happily recommend giving this one a look. I'd simply suggest keeping an eye out for a sale, where I think it becomes excellent value for money.

Artisan TD is a fantasy tower-defense-strategy game that does everything very well but not exceptionally well. Quite strategic with a use for every tower, but had way more emphasis on creating mazes with towers than other TD games I've seen. It was not a negative; it was even the original feature that made it stand out from the rest. The other thing being the limited quick shots, extra manual-fired shots, which I didn't care for. I appreciated the zoom feature. I wish more TD games had that. Several modern quality-of-life features that made the game more pleasant to play, such as being able to restart a wave you'd already done to do better. Attractive 3d graphics but the monsters were a little too detailed making them less distinguishable from each other especially when tower "light" effects were affecting them. The story was almost totally overlooked. No intro, no cinematics, no even illustrated panels between maps and just a paragraph of text when you finish it all. I prefer a little more gravy or sauce with my meat and potatoes. In later maps, it seemed selling the towers and replacing them from wave to wave became more necessary... and annoying. It became even worse with the bank giving 20% interest on the gold remaining at the end of a wave. The game is weirdly demanding for your GPU, so make sure you enable Vsync to avoid overheating. Even then, at the end of the very busy anniversary map, my computer "froze" even though I'm not sure of the cause. Overall, Artisan TD is a solid value for the price with 42 maps.

I got Artisan TD for free from Humble Bundle, and honestly put off playing it for a really long time because of the reviews. The TL;DR is I don't think it's quite worth the $16.99USD it's currently listed at, but I'd probably be willing to pay $10 for it. Pros: Cute art style, decent soundtrack, and 12-20 hours of gameplay if you play through once depending on how familiar with Tower Defence and Strategy you are. A lot of the reviews I read mentioned feeling like they were locked in to a certain style of play and that it was more of a puzzle with one right answer than anything else. This is kind of true if you're playing on Nightmare (the hardest difficulty), however if you play on any of the lower difficulties there's much more wiggle room in tower arrangement. Cons: Once all of the towers are unlocked, it's very repetitive, and once you get familiar with what towers to use for what kind of wave the difficulty falls off quite a bit. The first 5-6 hours of gameplay were very enjoyable, but the latter half it really felt like I was still playing just to complete the game more than because I was actually enjoying myself. There's the aroma of a story throughout, however it would be much more enjoyable if it had been fleshed out a little bit more. It's also designed for primarily mouse only input which can make certain actions very clunky - it simplifies the game which is nice, but for people familiar with the genre it'd be nice to have the option of more robust hotkeys. Overall I'd probably give it a 6/10. Worth playing the once, but I'll probably never touch it again.

I really enjoyed this game. It's very well balanced, easy to complete casually, and the hardest mode (nightmare) requires a good amount of thought and puzzle-solving for a perfect run. A couple of bugs here and there: twice I had to restart a level because the score became permanently offset even when restarting or rewinding the wave, and I had one achievement not unlock even though the requirements were met (twice). But overall, it's a smooth experience. If you like the tower defense genre, this one is worth picking up.

I wanted to take a quick minute to say if you like classic TD games this is it. It is a crafted TD experience. Offers max difficulty and has a built in modifier that gives more resources to help. If you are a fan of PixelJunk Monsters TD game this is a similar vein minus the controllable character. The focus is: mazing/labyrinth building, adjusting towers to waves, upgrade efficiency. In some cases, not sure what the shorthand of it is called but on that final big wave where you have to sell half your towers on the front side to handle the wave on the backside, there is a lot of that too. The tower upgrades are very linear too. You can feel the power increase and not get lost in what specific tower attribute to level. The lack of freedom here feels good. Also, ice towers are your friend. You basically have to weave them throughout your entire maze. All in all, I would say this is one of the best Humble Bundle games I have received. I am only about a 3rd of the way through and only a couple of levels I have reached true perfected on (Nightmare - no leak), but getting a perfect on Nightmare even with Prince feels just as well earned. Also another amazing feature is you can go back to a specific wave. There will be time I didn't notice I had a leak or my build order is not working and I can backup one wave at a time to find the leak and start from there. None of this "oh you had a leak, you have to start from wave 1 and waste 10min of your life to see if your new strategy will work 5 waves from now". This HEAVILY considers my time as a gamer dad that loves TD games. So this game is very CORE TD with quality of life considerations. I will buy EVERY TD this developer makes, full price even if they keep pumping them out. Part of me wouldn't mind if they keep things the same, just cosmetically different enemies/mechanics/towers, but wouldn't mind trying their take on some more progressive TD mechanics (rogue-like upgrade trees, tower fusions, separate base build concept).
